messages.author: 84799cd2e00b1b8d
messages.subject: Shared random effects model
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I'm trying to construct build a model where I evaluate 2 outcomes (y1 and y2) and connect them through two shared random effects (a spatially correlated one (v_i) and a spatially correlated one u_i)

So in short, I have these 2 models, whereby u_i and v_i are in common:
y1~intercept1+u_i+v_i
y2~intercept2+u_i+v_i

I had the following code, but the problem is that u_i and v_i are not the same, but they are coming from the same distribution:
formula1 = y1~ f(v_i,model="iid",param=c(0.5,0.008)) +
f(u_i,model="besag", graph=graph.loc, param=c(0.5,0.008), adjust.for.con.comp = FALSE)
formula2 = y2~ f(v_i,model="iid",param=c(0.5,0.008)) +
f(u_i,model="besag", graph=graph.loc, param=c(0.5,0.008), adjust.for.con.comp = FALSE)

Does anyone have an idea on how to say to inla that u_i and v_i have to be same over the 2 models?

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Shared random effects model
parts:
Hi, if they have the same likelihood, you can do

intercept = as.factor(rep(1:2, n))
ii = rep(1:n, 2)
jj = rep(1:n, 2)
yy = c(y1, y2)

formula = yy ~ -1 + intercept + f(ii,...) + f(jj,...)

if the likliehood, is different, do

YY = matrix(NA, 2*n, 2)
YY[1:n, 1] = y1
YY[1:n+n, 2] = y2

and YY ~ ....



for f(idx...), then idx[1] can appear many times, or not at all.

Best
H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Shared random effects model
parts:
Hi,

I have a follow-up question on the subject.
I'm still working with these 2 models:
y1 ~ intercept1 + u_i + v_i
y2 ~ intercept2 + u_i + v_i

Since the likelihoods are different, this has been modeled as followed in R:

formula = yy~ -1 + intercept + f(region.unstruct,model="iid",param=c(0.5,0.008)) +
f(region.struct,model="besag", graph=graph.loc, param=c(0.5,0.008), adjust.for.con.comp = FALSE)

intercept = as.factor(rep(1:2,each=nrow(data5)))
region.unstruct = rep(data5$index, 2)
region.struct = rep(data5$index, 2)
yy = matrix(NA, 2*nrow(data5), 2)
yy[1:nrow(data5), 1] = y1
yy[1:nrow(data5)+nrow(data5), 2] = y2
scale = c(data5$scale.y1, data5$scale.y2)


mod <- inla(formula, family = rep("gaussian", 2), data=data.frame(intercept, region.unstruct, region.struct, scale, yy), 
control.fixed=list(prec.intercept=1),
control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE,link=1),
control.family=list(list(hyper=list(prec=list(initial=log(1),fixed=TRUE))), list(hyper=list(prec=list(initial=log(1),fixed=TRUE)))),
scale=scale)


But now I want to allow for the fact y1 might be more prevalent than y2 (and this difference might be more variable than just intercept2-intercept1).

So we allow for the random effects  to vary a bit as follows using lambda1 and lambda2:
y1 ~ intercept1 + lambda1 * u_i + lambda2 * v_i
y2 ~ intercept2 + u_i + v_i

These lambdas can follow for example a normal distribution. 
Is there a way how i can adjust the code mentioned above for these lambdas?

Thanks in advance!

Kind regards,
Kevin
2017-06-27 11:04 GMT+02:00 Kevin WATJOU <kevin....@uhasselt.be>:

Hi,

This worked like a charm! Thank you!!

Kind regards

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Shared random effects model
parts:
The weights in 'copy' are default fixed to be 1 but you can set fixed=F
and then they will be estimated. Sometimes, its helps to know a little
bit of what you expect of them, like using an informative prior. you
can also set the range of those, to range=c(LOW, HIGH)

H

Hi,

Thank you for the reply. I have modelled the correlated random effect

y1 ~ intercept1 + lambda1 * u_i + lambda2 * v_i
y2 ~ intercept2 + u_i + v_i
as follows in in INLA using the copy function:
formula = yy~ -1 + intercept +

f(region.struct1,model="besag", graph=graph.loc, param=c(0.5,0.008), adjust.for.con.comp = FALSE) + 
f(region.struct2, lambda1, copy="region.struct1", fixed=F) + 
f(region.unstruct1,model="iid",param=c(0.5,0.008)) + 
f(region.unstruct2, lambda2, copy="region.unstruct1", fixed=F)

intercept = as.factor(rep(1:2,each=nrow(data5)))
region.unstruct = rep(data5$index, 2)
region.struct = rep(data5$index, 2)
yy = matrix(NA, 2*nrow(data5), 2)
yy[1:nrow(data5), 1] = y1
yy[1:nrow(data5)+nrow(data5), 2] = y2
scale = c(data5$scale.y1, data5$scale.y2)

lambda1 = c(rep(1, length(data5$index)),rep(NA, length(data5$index)))
lambda2 = c(rep(NA, length(data5$index)),rep(1, length(data5$index)))

mod <- inla(formula, family = rep("gaussian", 2), data=data.frame(intercept, region.unstruct, region.struct, scale, yy), 
control.fixed=list(prec.intercept=1),
control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE,link=1),
control.family=list(list(hyper=list(prec=list(initial=log(1),fixed=TRUE))), list(hyper=list(prec=list(initial=log(1),fixed=TRUE)))),
scale=scale)

Is there also a way to estimate these lambda-weights as such or are they estimated together with region.(un)struct2? Also, can i specify a prior on the lambda's themselves? Because, i think i'm specifying a prior on u_1 and v_i of y1 .

Thanks in advance!

Kind regards,
Kevin
2017-07-12 9:16 GMT+02:00 INLA help <he...@r-inla.org>:

The weights in 'copy' are default fixed to be 1 but you can set fixed=F
and then they will be estimated. Sometimes, its helps to know a little
bit of what you expect of them, like using an informative prior. you
can also set the range of those, to range=c(LOW, HIGH)

H

> control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE,link=1),
> control.family=list(list(hyper=list(prec=list(initial=l
> og(1),fixed=TRUE))),
> list(hyper=list(prec=list(initial=log(1),fixed=TRUE)))),
> scale=scale)
>
> Is there also a way to estimate these lambda-weights as such or are
> they estimated together with region.(un)struct2? Also, can i specify
> a prior on the lambda's themselves? Because, i think i'm specifying a
> prior on u_1 and v_i of y1 .

youre 'lambda's above will just be constants that scale u and v. if you want to
scale those again, like

beta * lambda1 * u_i

you can do 'fixed=F' as you do, but better to use the new style like

hyper = list(beta = list(
initial = 1,
prior = "normal",
param = c(1,10),
fixed = FALSE))

to give a normal prior for beta with mean 1 and precision 10.


Best
